facts.t: Appears in 0.06% of the 23,531 paintings in our archive (15 paintings, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 9).
In our 23,531-painting archive it is rarer than 66% of the named colors.

First seen in our archive in 1452 (commons-Q21729770, by Bartolomeo Caporali); the third-earliest painting is 1609, and the latest 1922 (9 dated paintings, at least 2% of the canvas, as photographed). The archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first. That is 503 years before the name's earliest record in our sources (1955): the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof of the pigment or dye.
In printed English the word peaks in the 1940s and rose fastest in the 1990s (Google Books, all senses of the word, so a color name that is also an object or a place can mislead).
